pr_title: fix(ivy): ensure that changes to component resources trigger incremental builds
pr_body:
Optimisations to skip compiling source files that had not changed
did not account for there being only changes to a resource file,
such as a template or style file.

Now we track such dependencies and trigger a recompilation
if any of the previously tracked resources have changed.

Closes #30947

issue_context.title: serve(aot): with Ivy, does not detect changes to files
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 Bug report ### Command ``` - [x] serve ``` ### Is this a regression? Yes? I didn't use AOT for dev mode serving previously because it wasn't as performant as it is now in Ivy. ### Description The [Ivy Guide](https://angular.io/guide/ivy) suggests enabling `"aot": true` for dev mode builds. What I’m finding during that experience is that while the rebuilds are super fast in Dev mode (`aot: true`), the Angular CLI often doesn’t pick up changes to SCSS and HTML. I need to constantly re-run `ng serve` over and over again to see my changes. It’s not the kind of DX that we’re looking for. Changing back to `aot: false` works around this issue. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction - https://github.com/angular-hispano/angular-hispano/tree/enableIvy - `npm start` - Make changes to files like the following and see that the build reports ```sh Date: 2019-06-09T02:07:26.153Z - Hash: fd4823b00365cd497714 - Time: 192ms 7 unchanged chunks ℹ ｢wdm｣: Compiled successfully. ``` But the changes aren't reflected in the browser. comments:
From debugging the linked repository, it appears that this line in the Ivy AOT compiler is causing the component file to be skipped: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/program.ts#L350

The root cause may be that that the template and style dependencies of a component are not accounted for in the incremental compilation checks for Ivy.
I think we missed testing for this on the CLI because we do e2e for ivy, but some of our tests (including the more elaborate rebuild ones) are not e2e.
Ahah! Yes, we do not include external template files as dependencies of a compiled file!
